newsitem.title: JAPAN: EMU should not be sole investment factor -- Nissan.
newsitem.headline: EMU should not be sole investment factor -- Nissan.

text.p: Nissan Motor Corp president Yoshikazu Hanawa said on Friday that his company's investment in Europe should be determined by various factors and not solely on the issue of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"Investment should determined by various factors, and whether Britain joins the EMU or not will not be the only factor for us to make the decision," Hanawa told reporters.
"It's up to Britain to decide whether it joins in the single currency," he added.
Nissan has already decided on its future investments in Europe and that will not change, Hanawa said.

Referring to comments made on Wednesday by Toyota Motor Corp president Hiroshi Okuda that Britain would be less attractive as a base if it was not in the EMU, Hanawa said he could not see how the rival carmaker could make its decisions on the EMU factor alone.

Nissan is seeking sales of over 500,000 cars as soon as possible after it starts production of its new model at its British unit, Yoshikazu Kawana, executive vice president in charge of overseas operations, told Reuters.
Earlier in January, Nissan announced it will invest a further 215 million sterling to start making the Almera car model by the year 2000 in its plant in Sunderland, northeast England.
"We sold 570,000 cars in 1992 and we wanted to bring our European sales back to that level as soon as possible," he said. "We're not happy with the 460,000 sold last year."

As a result of the new model at the British unit, 90 percent of Nissan's overall European car sales will be made by its European unit, and that will improve the financial condition of the unit substantially, he added.
